A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FEDGVI work. All 41 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are available and readable; the text, equations, tables, and rendered figures support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments and classification results on Covertype, MNIST, and Fashion MNIST, including additional analyses in Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix D, including accuracy, uncertainty, robustness, and runtime results.

M1.justification: The FEDGVI procedure, cavity distribution, client/server objectives, damping, and loss/divergence options are unchanged in Algorithms 1–2 and Equations (3)–(8). The theorem revisions do not change the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic location, outlier-influence, and logistic-regression tasks, plus Covertype, MNIST, and Fashion MNIST. No dataset, population, or contamination scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: PVI and MLE in Figure 2; PVI, FedAvg, DSGLD, and DSVGD in Figure 5; and the same neural-network comparators, including FedPA and beta-PredBayes, in Tables 1–3.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D retain the same splits, sample and client counts, contamination procedures, architectures, optimizers, learning rates, metrics, and best-iteration reporting. The revised appendix wording does not report changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: The influence analysis, loss/divergence sweep, architecture comparison, learning-rate study, local robustness-parameter sensitivity, and runtime analysis are already present in v2 and retained in v3, including Figures 3, 6, and 9–12 and Tables 3–5.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten Covertype train/test splits and five neural-network runs/seeds. Standard-deviation reporting and plotted uncertainty remain unchanged; no new statistical procedure or repetition information is introduced.

E6.justification: Corresponding numerical entries and plotted findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains combined-loss/divergence FEDGVI accuracies of 97.50 ± 0.07 and 98.13 ± 0.08 for ten and three clients, respectively.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.9 now explicitly requires recovery of the generalized Bayesian posterior as well as subsequent invariance. Appendix B.5 formalizes attainment at an iteration and aligns its stated assumptions with the main text. This is a limited formal refinement; the existing proof is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about robust probabilistic federated learning, recovery of existing methods, cavity necessity, conjugate updates, and empirical advantages.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 newly characterizes the robustness conditions as equivalent to gamma being bounded and integrable under the prior measure. This adds an interpretation of applicability, but its boundedness assertion is not generally equivalent to the retained condition bounding pi*gamma. Other interpretations and limitations are unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, data-generation instructions, and printed code-access information remain unchanged. The code URL is merely placed on a separate line in Appendix D.

R1.justification: v3 adds Blei et al. (2017), cites it alongside the already-listed Walker (2013) in Appendix C.3, and explicitly attributes the objective identity in Appendix B.3.1 to an analogue of Ashman et al.'s Property 2. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes limited grammar and capitalization corrections, expands introductory explanations in the proofs, and adds cross-references and notation guidance. The main narrative and section organization remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The same twelve figures and six tables remain. v3 reflows appendix content, changes the supplementary opening layout, adds integral-grouping delimiters in Appendix B.7, and slightly expands Table 5's caption. No plot or table is added or substantively redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the precision of Theorem 4.9 and its appendix assumptions, with modest gains in exposition and attribution. However, Appendix C.2 introduces an inaccurate equivalence: bounding pi*gamma does not generally require gamma itself to be bounded under the prior. With the empirical evidence unchanged, these clarification gains and the new mathematical misstatement leave the net overall quality direction uncertain.
